last_result.headline: Q44 (run after Q45, because its own turn died on an API-529 with no work done) modelled the DRAW instead of a point estimate, because best-of-2 keeps the BETTER of the two selected on private, so a pair's value is E[min] and its risk is that minimum's tail. Cross-family difference sd 2.40, calibrated from Q18's 29% reversal at a 1.328 gap and independently corroborated by the ledger's measured 2.54 ft output disagreement; degeneracy control reproduces Q53's +0.0005 at draw scale 0. HEADLINE: the SECOND SLOT is the largest positive term in the decision -- a diverse pair is worth -0.456 mean / -0.939 p95 versus its slot-1 alone, a second frontier member only -0.060 / -0.074, and the entire slot-1 dispute is bounded at 0.077. Best-of-2 is a call option on variance, so decorrelation and draw uncertainty both ADD value. WHATEVER HAPPENS IN SLOT 1, 54844628 HOLDS SLOT 2. DELIVERABLE: score-first's discriminator is BELOW the measured resolution -- its 0.080 public gap is 2.7 sd of Q45's 0.03 floor, and the only resolvable component (GR-sigma -0.1105) is the one Q36 measured on 760 wells as helping just 42.1% of wells with a negative median. The two pairs are tied ON MEASUREMENT, so the tie breaks on ownership/verifiability: 54968060+54844628 is at least as good and strictly better in 8 of 24 cells. Two axes the task asked to stress do NOT discriminate: dependency risk (both pairs carry identical dependency sets, and neither slot is dependency-free) and draw representativeness (gap <=0.001 at every scale). Teammate-provenance loss costs ~0.004 and its optimum is pair B.
